facts.statement: Picrocleidus lived during the Middle Jurassic Callovian stage in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Picrocleidus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Middle Jurassic Oxford Clay Formation (Callovian stage) of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in Peterborough, England, and acquired by Alfred Nicholson Leeds.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in the Oxford Clay Formation in Peterborough, England and acquired by Alfred Nicholson Leeds.

facts.statement: The species name beloclis means "arrow clavicle" because the interclavicle bone was triangular.
facts.quote: The specific name means "arrow clavicle", referring to the triangular interclavicula.

facts.statement: Charles William Andrews established the genus Picrocleidus in 1910.
facts.quote: M. beloclis was moved to its own genus Picrocleidus by Charles William Andrews in 1910.

facts.statement: Five specimens of Picrocleidus are currently known to science.
One known specimen includes a complete skeleton with a skull and a full tail.
facts.quote: Specimen BMNH R3698, a skeleton with skull, including a complete tail.

facts.statement: A young individual of the species is represented by a known fossil specimen.
Picrocleidus is classified as a member of the family Cryptoclididae.
facts.quote: Picrocleidus is currently classified as a member of the Cryptoclididae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Picrocleidus is synonymous with the genus Muraenosaurus.
facts.quote: Picrocleidus has previously been considered synonymous with Muraenosaurus although there are doubts in the relationship between the two groupings.

facts.statement: Picrocleidus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)
